Via-Invest werd hiertoe op 9 mei 2017 omgevormd in een naamloze vennootschap van publiek recht, genoemd “De Werkvennootschap”, die als projecteigenaar meer slagkracht zal hebben. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. GENERAL INFORMATION In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 7.107-5 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 205.205-70, this serves as public notification that Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk, Contracting Department, on behalf of the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) and the Naval Intelligence Activity (NIA), intends to consolidate and bundle requirements for Enterprise-Wide Information Technology (EWIT) Support Services into a single contract action. The proposed acquisition strategy is currently under evaluation and being finalized by the Government. Sourcing options and potential contract vehicles are still being actively reviewed to ensure the final strategy maximizes efficiency while preserving competitive opportunities to the greatest extent practicable. The resulting contract structure is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) vehicle consisting of a five-year lifecycle (one-year base period plus four one-year option periods). To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers.
